data.source: AMIS belt median via Kissan Cares

data.title: AMIS maize 26 Nov: belt median edges up to Rs6,438 per 100 kg with all nine belt mandis reporting; Burewala slips to Rs5,938
data.summary: Belt median Rs6,438 per 100 kg (Rs2,575 per 40 kg) on 26 Nov vs Rs6,406 on 25 Nov, with Arifwala back at Rs6,500; Burewala fell to Rs5,938 (from Rs6,125) and Sahiwal stayed lowest at Rs4,650. Other Punjab mandis median rose to Rs7,625 on seven mandis (TT Singh Rs10,250, Lodhran Rs5,625).

data.act: Keep buying dry new-crop in weekly lots, starting with Sahiwal (Rs46.5/kg for a sixth report, check moisture on such a low price), then Burewala (Rs59.4/kg, down from Rs61.3/kg), Pakpattan (Rs63.5/kg), Vehari (Rs63.8/kg) and Mailsi (Rs64.4/kg); Arifwala and Chichawatni are Rs65.0/kg, Kamalia Rs68.8/kg and Okara Rs74.8/kg. Reject lots above 14% moisture or failing aflatoxin.
data.why: The belt median was Rs64.4/kg on 26 Nov with all nine belt mandis reporting, up 0.5% from Rs64.1/kg on 25 Nov; it is level with 27 Oct (Rs64.4/kg), 19.5% below a year ago (Rs80.0/kg on 26 Nov 2025) and at 36% of its 52-week range (Rs54.4–82.5/kg). Other Punjab mandis firmed to a Rs76.3/kg median, so the belt stays the cheapest source as autumn-crop arrivals peak in Nov–Dec.

data.refreshNote: Added AMIS maize for 26 Nov (belt median Rs6,438 per 100 kg, +0.5%, nine mandis; other Punjab Rs7,625) and refreshed the maize view; wheat 26 Nov was already in, rice rows are generic paddy, CBOT has not traded since 25 Nov (Thanksgiving), the 26 Nov interbank close was not found (Business Recorder pages failed) and the PBS urea week to 26 Nov is not out yet.
